title: Countdown Timer
story: 3... 2... 1... Launch! Countdowns create anticipation. Whether it's a New Year's Eve countdown, a pomodoro work timer, or a rocket launch, the countdown is universal. Build a timer that ticks down from any duration, displaying minutes and seconds.
why: A countdown timer teaches time decomposition (hours/minutes/seconds), decrementing state, formatted display, and loop-based tick simulation.
analogy: A kitchen timer shaped like a tomato (pomodoro!). Twist the dial to 25 minutes, and it ticks down second by second until DING. Your countdown timer is the digital version: set hours, minutes, seconds; press start; watch the numbers descend. When it hits zero, the alarm (print) fires.
try_it: Add hours to the display (HH:MM:SS). Add pause/resume functionality. Implement a lap timer that records split times. Add an alarm sound by printing 'BEEP!' repeatedly. Create multiple timers running simultaneously.
tips: Store time in seconds — convert to HH:MM:SS only for display
Pad single digits with leading zero for proper time display
common_mistakes: Ticking past zero — check remaining > 0 BEFORE decrementing
Forgetting to update the display after each tick — timer appears frozen
Mixing up minutes and seconds in the format string
